rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination - source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 HUD voucher holder the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of income.
rules.coverage_text: Sale or rental of all property, including open land, whether for business or residential purposes, subject to listed exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as a residence; rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as a residence; preference given to persons of the same religion by a religious organization.
rules.penalty: A complaint may be filed with the Division on Civil Rights for free within 180 days of the alleged violation, or in New Jersey Superior Court within two years of the alleged violation.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
